record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds
record.original_question: Let M be a closed smooth aspherical 4-manifold. Is every smooth 4-manifold that is homotopy equivalent to M necessarily diffeomorphic to M?

evidence.quote: Question. Let M be a closed smooth aspherical 4-manifold. Is every smooth 4-manifold homotopy equivalent to M diffeomorphic to M? The question has not been answered for any M, not even the 4-torus.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a closed smooth aspherical 4-manifold (i.e., $M$ is a closed connected smooth manifold of dimension 4 whose universal cover is contractible). Is every closed smooth 4-manifold $N$ that is homotopy equivalent to $M$ necessarily diffeomorphic to $M$? In particular, resolve the case $M = T^4$, the 4-dimensional torus.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint "Exotic aspherical 4-manifolds" (Davis–Hayden–Huang–Ruberman–Sunukjian, arXiv:2411.19400) constructs closed aspherical smooth 4-manifolds that are homeomorphic (hence homotopy equivalent) but not diffeomorphic, refuting the smooth Borel conjecture in dimension 4. This answers the general question in the negative, but the question remains open for many specific aspherical 4-manifolds, including the 4-torus $T^4$.

status_evidence.title: Exotic aspherical 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: We construct closed, aspherical, smooth 4-manifolds that are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic, providing counterexamples to a smooth analog of the Borel conjecture in dimension four.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples to smooth Borel conjecture in dim 4 exist, but not for the 4-torus.

status_evidence.title: Aspherical manifolds - Manifold Atlas
status_evidence.snippet: The Borel Conjecture is false in the smooth category.
status_evidence.claim: Smooth Borel rigidity fails in general; status in dimension 4 had been a long-standing question.
